text:
Jake Sanderson came back into a winning team and has helped keep it that way. He plays nearly 25 minutes a night, and the Senators take 53% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five with him on the ice. He is one of the league's best skaters by NHL Edge (top speed in the 100th percentile) with a 99 mph shot.

What's missing is the production. He is pointless in six straight, but on 4.7 expected points' worth of on-ice chances, so the looks are there; it's the finishing around him and his own shot (3.3% shooting) that have gone cold. Ten points in 14 games is still a fine pace for a defenseman.

The bigger picture is why Ottawa built around him. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.3 wins last season, fifth among 215 defensemen, much of it on the power play, with the caveat that he plays beside strong teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than almost any defenseman. Watch for the points to catch up.
